layers.title: Native clients
layers.requirement: Run coding and bounded research with existing native accounts, client tools, model choices and resumable sessions.
layers.current_choice: Native Codex and Claude Code; application SDKs only for a demonstrated application requirement.

layers.title: Workers and task ownership
layers.requirement: Delegate bounded independent work, preserve owned edits and actual failed results, and integrate only after relevant review.
layers.current_choice: Native Claude/Codex workers with owned Worktrunk worktrees; optional Beads when dependency tracking is needed, optional qualified cross-client review and an opt-in semantic-evidence-reviewer with explicit TypeSafe context.
layers.rationale: Native writing, review and selected-child recovery have returned evidence without another orchestration runtime. Worktrunk's actual old/new comparison corrected child working-directory behavior. Durable cross-host effects would require a different acceptance boundary.
limitations: Graceful native Workflow resume is separate from the systemd child-crash fixture; neither transfers every hard-crash guarantee to the other.
The restricted reviewer tool profile is not the accepted inherited-tool lane. The older companion backend acceptance does not certify every outer plugin invocation.
Native model/effort settings are inherited and returned identities recorded. Skill propagation is not a universal runtime/model ranking; account scopes and failed read paths remain evidence.

The September 21 New York / September 22 UTC source refresh adds Deep Agents, OpenHands SDK/Agent Canvas, Microsoft Agent Framework and DeerFlow comparisons. It does not install them or establish a head-to-head worker winner; historical DeerFlow adapter evidence applies only to its recorded revision.
layers.overturn_when: A real task needs durable multi-host state, approval waits or effect recovery beyond native workers, and one challenger passes frozen cancellation, replay, ownership and integration cases.

candidates.rationale: Owned native children and graceful workflow recovery have actual retained results; use the qualified role/tool configuration.

layers.verdict_overturn_when:
The verdict changes in three cases.

1. A real task needs durable multi-host state, approval waits or effect recovery beyond what native workers provide. A challenger (Deep Agents, OpenHands SDK, LangGraph or Temporal) would then have to pass the same frozen cases as the native arms: cancellation, same-identity continuation, parent-crash containment, an unchanged checkpoint with exactly one effect, and owned-file repair verified by frozen tests. The frozen inputs are blueprints/convergence-practice/worker-recovery/native-exact-read-plan.json and native-exact-read-freeze.json, the receipt is native-exact-read-receipt.json, and the owned-file cases are blueprints/convergence-practice/native-worker/plan.json and checks.json. The challenger must match or beat the native Claude and Codex arms, with complete usage retained.

2. c11 is demoted to a review-only role if a Codex native worker run on the native-worker fixture (plan.json/checks.json) fails the owned-file repair.

3. The Worktrunk default changes if a crash-cleanup test removes unrelated or dirty state.

layers.title: Isolation
layers.requirement: Separate edits and apply a real filesystem/network boundary only where the selected task requires enforced restrictions.
layers.current_choice: Worktrunk/Git worktrees for edit ownership and sandbox-runtime for qualified Linux restrictions. Apple Container remains conditional on an eligible macOS host and a matching container requirement.
layers.rationale: These mechanisms cover different requirements: worktrees separate changes, while accepted sandbox profiles enforce selected access rules. A managed VM or OCI platform adds a separate deployment boundary that the bounded native workload does not currently need.
limitations: A worktree is not a security sandbox. Ordinary native or Dagu processes are not automatically sandboxed.
Selected access/network fixtures do not certify hostile workloads, resource limits or unsupported platforms.
layers.overturn_when: Untrusted code or a deployment target requires a stronger VM/OCI boundary, and the selected alternative passes workload, network, resource, cleanup and host compatibility checks.

layers.title: Context and usage efficiency
layers.requirement: Supply useful task context with recoverable originals and measure artifact reductions separately from provider usage.
layers.current_choice: Focused reads and scoped retrieval first; task-selected RTK, Context Mode and explicit-file Repomix; optional guarded Headroom and TOON only after a suitable same-artifact comparison; ccusage observes native usage.
layers.rationale: Scoped functional results and retained losing comparisons support selective activation. The older fixed-order provider trial reduced Codex usage 11.26% but increased Claude 25.83%; uncontrolled caching and plugin absence prevent causal savings claims.

TOON expands the full catalog relative to compact JSON; guarded compression must return originals on rejection. Exact whole-PC lifetime savings are unmeasured.
layers.overturn_when: A frozen task/artifact and repeated controlled comparison improves answer correctness or retrieval completeness while reducing complete provider use or latency, with successful raw-input recovery.

None of the retained evidence shows it covering permission scoping, pin enforcement, inventory or attribution. It is a complementary correctness gate next to zizmor, not a winner for this requirement's parts.

alternatives.why_not_default: Hosted initial scans 35541330440 and 35541327481 succeeded and opened major proposals #29 and #30. Their hash failures correctly blocked integration (catalogs/foundation/automation.json lines 32-36; docs/github-automation.md lines 56-62). It keeps GitHub Actions SHA pins current but does not detect or enforce unpinned uses. It owns only GitHub Actions references: pip is not activated, and the curl-downloaded binaries are outside its scope (docs/github-automation.md lines 375-404). Weekly timing and a nonempty minor/patch group are unobserved (automation.json lines 264-266).

alternatives.why_not_default: Native gitleaks accepted clean controls and rejected inert fixtures (catalogs/foundation/decisions.json, offline-security-inventory). Its capability is secret detection, which is the secrets-credentials layer's concern (decisions.json secrets-credentials-policy, review_status source_review with no new execution). The hosted secret-scan evidence is incomplete: the first hosted run was cancelled by its own timeout during the history scan (docs/github-automation.md lines 465-469). secret-scan is named only in the committed ruleset, not the applied one (lines 296-302). The sources conflict on its failure policy: automation.json says no fail threshold has been decided, while github-automation.md lines 296-298 says the job fails on any detection.
